# 1 Samuel Chapter 19 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 161v-162r | **Source Image:** 1SA_019_page_001.jpg, 1SA_019_page_002.jpg

---

**19:1** And-Saul-spoke to Jonathan his-son and-to all his-servants to-put-David-to-death. And-Jonathan, son of-Saul, delighted in-David exceedingly.

**19:2** And-Jonathan-told to-David, saying, "Saul my-father [is]-seeking to-put-you-to-death. And-now, be-on-guard, please, in-the-morning, and-dwell in-a-secret-place and-hide-yourself.

**19:3** And-I will-go-out and-stand beside my-father in-the-field where you [are], and-I will-speak concerning-you to my-father, and-I-will-see what [there is], and-I-will-tell to-you."

**19:4** And-Jonathan-spoke good concerning-David to Saul his-father, and-said to-him, "Let-not the-king sin against his-servant, against-David, for he-has-not sinned against-you, and-for his-deeds [are] very good to-you.

**19:5** And-he-put his-life [nefesh] in-his-hand, and-he-struck the-Philistine, and-YHWH-worked a-great salvation [teshuʿah] for-all Israel. You-saw and-you-rejoiced; and-why will-you-sin against-innocent blood, to-put-David-to-death without-cause?"

**19:6** And-Saul-listened to-[the]-voice of-Jonathan, and-Saul-swore, "[As]-YHWH lives, he-shall-not be-put-to-death."

**19:7** And-Jonathan-called to-David, and-Jonathan-told to-him all these words. And-Jonathan-brought David to Saul, and-he-was before-him as-yesterday-[and]-the-day-before.

**19:8** And-the-war-continued again, and-David-went-out and-fought against-the-Philistines, and-struck among-them [a]-great striking, and-they-fled from-his-face.

**19:9** And-an-evil spirit of-YHWH was upon Saul, and-he [was]-sitting in-his-house, and-his-spear [was] in-his-hand, and-David [was]-playing with-[his]-hand.

**19:10** And-Saul-sought to-strike the-spear through-David and-through-the-wall, and-he-slipped-away from-[the]-face of-Saul, and-he-struck the-spear into-the-wall. And-David fled and-escaped on-that night.

**19:11** And-Saul-sent messengers to [the]-house of-David, to-watch-him and-to-put-him-to-death in-the-morning. And-Michal his-wife told to-David, saying, "If you [do]-not save your-life [nefesh] tonight, tomorrow you [will be]-put-to-death."

**19:12** And-Michal-let-David-down through the-window, and-he-went and-fled and-escaped.

**19:13** And-Michal-took the-teraphim [household-idol] and-put [it] on the-bed, and-a-quilt [kevir] of-goats' [hair] she-put at-its-head, and-covered [it] with-the-garment.

**19:14** And-Saul-sent messengers to-take David, and-she-said, "He [is]-sick."

**19:15** And-Saul-sent the-messengers to-see David, saying, "Bring-him-up to-me in-the-bed, to-put-him-to-death."

**19:16** And-the-messengers-came, and-behold, the-teraphim [was] on the-bed, and-the-quilt of-goats' [hair] at-its-head.

**19:17** And-Saul-said to Michal, "Why thus have-you-deceived-me, and-sent my-enemy away, and-he-escaped?" And-Michal-said to Saul, "He said to-me, 'Send-me-away; why should-I-put-you-to-death?'"

**19:18** And-David fled and-escaped, and-came to Samuel, to-Ramah, and-told to-him all that Saul had-done to-him. And-he-went, he and-Samuel, and-they-dwelt in-Naioth [Navoth].

**19:19** And-it-was-told to-Saul, saying, "Behold, David [is] in-Naioth in-Ramah."

**19:20** And-Saul-sent messengers to-take David, and-they-saw [the]-assembly of-the-prophets prophesying [nibbeim], and-Samuel standing stationed over-them. And-[the]-spirit of-God was upon [the]-messengers of-Saul, and-they-also prophesied [vayitnabbe'u].

**19:21** And-they-told to-Saul, and-he-sent other messengers, and-they-also prophesied. And-Saul-continued and-sent messengers [a]-third [time], and-they-also prophesied.

**19:22** And-he-also-went to Ramah, and-came to [the]-great cistern that [is] in-Secu. And-he-asked and-said, "Where [are] Samuel and-David?" And-[one]-said, "Behold, in-Naioth in-Ramah."

**19:23** And-he-went there, to Naioth in-Ramah, and-[the]-spirit of-God was upon him, also-him, and-he-went walking and-prophesying until he-came to-Naioth in-Ramah.

**19:24** And-he-also stripped-off his-garments, and-he-also prophesied before Samuel, and-fell-down naked all that day and-all that night. Therefore they-say, "Is Saul also among-the-prophets [hannevi'im]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **19:5 -- "his-life in-his-hand"** (nafsho bekhapo): An idiom meaning to risk one's life. The nefesh (soul/life) placed literally in the palm -- suggesting total vulnerability and willingness to die.

2. **19:9 -- "evil spirit of-YHWH"**: The Leningrad Codex reads ruach YHWH raʿah, attributing the spirit directly to YHWH. Some manuscripts and LXX read "evil spirit of God" (Elohim). The MT consistently attributes both good and evil spirits to YHWH's sovereign will.

3. **19:13 -- teraphim** (teraphim): Household idol(s), here singular in function despite the plural form. That Michal had teraphim in David's house is noteworthy -- it suggests persistence of folk-religious practice within Israelite households. The object was apparently human-sized or large enough to simulate a body in bed.

4. **19:13 -- kevir** (kevir): This rare word occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Usually rendered "quilt," "pillow," or "net of goats' hair." The Leningrad Codex is clear on the consonantal text. The exact nature of this object remains debated.

5. **19:18 -- Naioth** (Navoth/Naioth): The Leningrad Codex ketiv is navith. This may be a proper place name or may derive from naveh ("habitation/pasture"), suggesting a prophetic settlement or encampment near Ramah. LXX transliterates variously.

6. **19:24 -- "naked"** (ʿarom): This likely means "stripped of outer garments" rather than completely unclothed. The same word is used of prophetic ecstasy. That Saul lay exposed "all that day and all that night" before Samuel underscores the totality of God's spirit overcoming his murderous intent.

7. **19:24 -- "Is Saul also among the prophets?"**: This is the second etiology for this proverbial saying (cf. 1 Sam 10:11-12). In ch. 10 it was ambiguously positive; here it is deeply ironic -- Saul's prophetic seizure prevents him from killing David.
